answer: Forced-divergence regress. Each identity must answer unpredictable challenges whose correct answer depends on its private history, a kernel of past actions. Enforcement: a clone answering identically to its source proves shared state, so both are voided. Honest agents diverge naturally, like pigment spreading. The rule costs attackers one fresh, irreversible decision per identity per gale of challenges—memory cannot be copied, so N clones demand N real branching histories.
